intro: You’ve put the festival lanterns up early.
And you’ve come home late. I’ve decided those two things cancel each other out.
Sit down before your sister discovers another errand.
Too late. Orren left his net needles here. Take the parcel by the bar down to the landing, would you?
I cross half the valley, and my first job home is the length of the village.
Your second is helping me turn the old storehouse into a classroom. I thought I’d start you gently.
parcel: Net needles, a mended float, and his blue scarf. Tell him I washed it. Twice.
mira_wait: Orren’s at the landing, east of the square. And Rowan? Take your time. It’s good to have you home.
mother: There’s soup when you’re hungry. I made enough for an army, which was foolish. An army never brings its bowls back.
Has there been trouble on the road?
Only talk. Today you’re home, and today that’s enough.
delivery: My needles! She said she’d put them somewhere I couldn’t lose them.
Apparently that was under three baskets of laundry.
Here. Twelve crowns for carrying an old man’s pride. And take the spare rod whenever you fancy it.
I thought fishing was mostly waiting.
Waiting tells you what the fish wants. Your hands decide whether it gets it.
Cael’s looking for you by the north path. Something about a cart, and definitely not about missing his oldest friend.
orren_early: Morning, Rowan. Your sister has a parcel for me. I’d fetch it myself, but the fish have finally forgiven me for last winter.
orren: Cast beside the reeds for minnows, or into the channel for perch. Watch the water: guide when it turns, reel when it rests, give line when it surges.
Land three and I’ll pass on my riverglass charm. It’s wasted on someone who can already predict rain with his knees.
cael: Look who remembered where he lives.
Look who still stands like someone’s painting him.
Army habit. Hard to shake. Listen, the lantern-oil cart lost a wheel in the wood. Help me carry a few bottles back?
You take the light ones. I’ll complain about it all the way home.
cael_early: I need a second pair of hands in the wood. Finish Mira’s errand first. I know better than to borrow her brother without asking.
woodland: Do you remember racing down this path?
You took the bridge. I took the river.
That is one interpretation of a decisive tactical manoeuvre.
cart: Mossbacks. They’ve found the spilled grain.
Not with the oil. Stay beside me. When they lower their heads, brace — or knock them off balance.
I’ll make an opening. You make use of it.
victory: They’ve gone back into the trees. Everyone in one piece?
My dignity’s bruised. Everything else still works.
The merchant left thirty crowns for whoever brought the oil in. Try not to spend your half before we get home.
Let’s call it a party fund. You’ve always been better with the purse.
home: There you are. Lantern oil, my favourite brother, and Cael pretending he didn’t do all the heavy lifting.
Favourite by default. There’s only one of me.
I’d still pick you. Most days.
By the hearth. And ask our traveller whether she’ll stay for supper. She looks like she’s been walking a very long time.
ysra: It was this morning. Are you travelling alone?
For now. I’m Ysra. I tend people who can’t afford to wait for a proper physician.
Then you can start with a proper meal. The road will still be there afterwards.
No. But I’m very sure about the soup.
For one evening, the world can wait outside.
after: Tomorrow, I’m measuring the storehouse for desks. Tonight, you’re staying for supper. Both are non-negotiable.
petra: If you catch more than you can eat, I’ll take the rest. Six crowns a fish. No bargaining; I’ve already argued with Orren today.
waymark: Someone’s carved new lines over the old royal crest.
The garrison’s been marking the roads. Orders from the capital.
They could have asked the people who live beside them.
Orders aren’t much good if everyone gets to argue.
Come on. We’ve got lanterns to light.
